{"concepts_used":["GC-0072"],"decline_reason":"","declined":false,"citations":[{"ref":"TMM/Part5/x-word-constituents/letters","quote":"To indicate a letter or letters the constituent LTR is used."},{"ref":"TMM/Part5/x-word-constituents/letters","quote":"Where there is a single letter in the trade mark, # is added to the constituents as well as LTR."},{"ref":"TMM/Part5/x-word-constituents/letters","quote":"A constituent with an equals sign prefix is added to the constituent for groups of letters. It is useful in enabling searchers to distinguish between a group of letters and the same letters used as a word."},{"ref":"TMM/Part5/x-word-constituents/letters","quote":"In addition, when a group of letters is clearly an acronym, although it spells a word, it is indexed as letters."}],"answer":"Under the Manual’s search-indexing practice (not legislation), single letters, letter groups and acronyms are recorded as follows [TMM/Part5/x-word-constituents/letters]:

- Letters generally: the constituent LTR identifies a letter or letters.
- Single letters: # is added to the constituents as well as LTR.
- Groups of letters: an additional constituent prefixed with an equals sign (=) is used, allowing searchers to distinguish the letter group from the same letters used as a word.
- Clear acronyms: these are indexed as letters even if they spell a word, so the letter-group indexing applies."}
